'''Gregory Walter Graffin''' (born November 6, 1964) is an American singer who is the lead vocalist and only constant member of the [[punk rock|punk]] band [[Bad Religion]], which he co-founded in 1980. He has also released three solo albums. 

Graffin obtained his [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] in zoology at [[Cornell University]] and has lectured courses in [[natural sciences]] both at the [[University of California, Los Angeles]] and at [[Cornell University]].

Graffin was born in Madison, Wisconsin, and spent part of his childhood in Milwaukee and Racine. He later moved with his family to California, where his mother settled in the San Fernando Valley. Graffin became involved in the emerging Southern California punk scene during his teenage years.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2013-02-26 |title=Punk Rock Origins: The Story Behind Bad Religion |url=https://www.pbssocal.org/shows/artbound/punk-rock-origins-the-story-behind-bad-religion |access-date=2026-10-18 |website=PBS SoCal |language=en}}</ref>

==Career==
===Bad Religion===

In 1980, at the age of 15, Graffin and a few high school classmates formed Bad Religion in Southern California's [[San Fernando Valley]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.thebrpage.net/theanswer/?article=bad%5Freligion%5F%28name%29 |title=Bad Religion (name) &#124; The Answer &#124; The Bad Religion Page - Since 1995 |publisher=Thebrpage.net |access-date=2021-11-07 |archive-date=November 7, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211107150426/https://www.thebrpage.net/theanswer/?article=bad_religion_(name) |url-status=dead }}</ref> After making a name for themselves in the Los Angeles punk scene, releasing two EPs and two full-length albums, they disbanded around 1985. However, Bad Religion reformed in 1986 with a new line-up, consisting of Graffin on vocals, [[Brett Gurewitz]] and [[Greg Hetson]] on guitars, [[Jay Bentley]] on bass, and [[Pete Finestone]] on drums. In 1988, they released ''[[Suffer (album)|Suffer]]'', which was a comeback for Bad Religion as well as a watershed for the [[Punk rock in California|Southern California punk]] sound popularized by guitarist Gurewitz's [[Epitaph Records]]. The reunion line-up made two more records before Finestone left the band in 1991.

Bad Religion has been known for its articulate and often politically charged lyrics as well as its fast-paced [[harmony]], [[melody]] and [[counterpoint]]. Graffin and Gurewitz are the band's two main songwriters, though Graffin wrote the bulk of the material on his own for a three-album period in the late 1990s. Gurewitz had left the band in 1994 to concentrate on the future of Epitaph.
[[file:Greg Graffin-Starland BallRoom-2007.jpg|thumb|upright|Graffin with Bad Religion in 2007 at the [[Starland Ballroom]], New Jersey]]
After a stint with major label [[Atlantic Records]] ended in the early 2000s, Bad Religion re-signed with Epitaph, and Gurewitz rejoined. They have since continued to co-write songs and recorded six records: ''[[The Process of Belief]]'' (2002), ''[[The Empire Strikes First]]'' (2004), ''[[New Maps of Hell (Bad Religion album)|New Maps of Hell]]'' (2007), ''[[The Dissent of Man]]'' (2010),<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.thebrpage.net/news/?newsID=1840 |title=New album title revealed! |publisher=Thebrpage.net |access-date=2010-10-07}}</ref> ''[[True North (Bad Religion album)|True North]]'' (2013), and their latest, ''[[Age of Unreason (album)|Age of Unreason]]'' (2019)

===Solo career===
Graffin recorded a solo album in 1997, called ''[[American Lesion]]'', which consisted of softer, more pop-oriented folk songs. Most of this album was written during the breakup of his marriage, and the songs reflect this in lyrics and style.

In 2005, Graffin recorded his second solo album, ''[[Cold as the Clay]].'' The album is an amalgamation of new songs by Graffin and 18th- and 19th-century American folk songs. It was produced by [[Brett Gurewitz]] and released via [[Anti- (record label)|ANTI-]] on July 10, 2006.

In a September 2015 interview, Graffin said that he had been working on his third solo album, on which he planned to continue the folk style of ''Cold as the Clay''. That record, ''Millport'', was released on March 10, 2017. It was co-written and produced by Gurewitz and features members of [[Social Distortion]] as backing musicians.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.thebrpage.net/news/?newsID=2151 |title=New solo album Greg Graffin? |publisher=The Bad Religion Page |date=26 September 2015 |access-date=2 October 2015 |archive-date=December 15, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181215121823/http://www.thebrpage.net/news/?newsID=2151 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Academics==
Graffin attended [[El Camino Real High School]], then obtained both his [[Bachelor of Arts|BA]] Biology, [[Bachelor of Science|BS]] Geology and [[Master of Science|master's]] in Geology at the [[University of California, Los Angeles]] (UCLA). In 2003 he went on to earn his PhD in Zoology from [[Cornell University]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://evolution-institute.org/profile/greg-graffin/|title=Greg Graffin|website=The Evolution Institute|language=en-US|access-date=2020-02-14|archive-date=June 21, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200621150453/https://evolution-institute.org/profile/greg-graffin/|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Liebig |first=Bethany |date=November 30, 2011 |title=Punk rocker becomes lecturer, preaching evolution {{!}} Cornell Chronicle |url=https://news.cornell.edu/stories/2011/11/bad-religion-punk-rocker-now-evolution-lecturer |access-date=2025-01-23 |website=news.cornell.edu |language=en}}</ref> The PhD dissertation was supervised by [[William B. Provine]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Graffin|first=Greg|title=The Cornell Evolution Project|url=http://www.polypterus.com/|access-date=June 5, 2013|url-status=dead|archive-date=September 12, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170912214459/http://polypterus.com/}}</ref> After years of being out-of-print, the title of his dissertation changed to "Evolution and Religion: Questioning the Beliefs of the World's Eminent Evolutionists".<ref>{{cite web |url=https://catalog.library.cornell.edu/cgi-bin/Pwebrecon.cgi?BBID=5077552 |title=Cornell University Library Catalog |url-status=dead |access-date=June 7, 2013 |archive-date=June 28, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170628165002/https://catalog.library.cornell.edu/cgi-bin/Pwebrecon.cgi?BBID=5077552 }}</ref>

Graffin returned to UCLA where he taught natural science courses.<ref name="Reading">{{cite web|last=Feinberg|first=Paul|title=Reading, Writing and Rock 'n' Roll|url=https://magazine.ucla.edu/exclusives/bad-religion_greg-graffin/|work=UCLA Magazine|access-date=June 23, 2012}}</ref> In a June 2008 interview with Bad Religion bassist [[Jay Bentley]], he mentioned that Graffin would be teaching there from January to March 2009.<ref>{{cite web|url= http://www.punknews.org/article/29193 |title=Bad Religion looks ahead to 2009 album |date=June 8, 2008 |work=Punknews.org|access-date=2010-10-07}}</ref> In April 2011, Graffin said that he would return to [[Cornell University]] that fall to co-teach for 14 weeks.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.thebrpage.net/news/?newsID=1913 |title=UPDATE: Bad Religion to be playing the Punk Rock Holiday Festival |work=Thebrpage.net |access-date=2012-05-12 |archive-date=August 19, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180819083113/http://www.thebrpage.net/news/?newsID=1913 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

In 2011 the new [[type species]] ''[[Qiliania]] graffini'' of an extinct bird from the lower [[Cretaceous]] was named after Graffin "for his contributions to evolutionary biology, his public out-reach through music, and his inspiration to young scientists around the world".<ref name=Qiliania>{{cite journal |last1=Ji |first1=Shu-An |last2= Atterholt |first2 = Jessie |last3 = O'Connor | first3= Jingmai | last4 = Lamanna |first4 = Matthew | last5 = Harris | first5 = Jerry |first6 = Da-Qing |last6 = Li |first7 = Hai-Lu | last7 = You | last8= Dodson |first8 = Peter |year=2011 |title=A new, three-dimensionally preserved enantiornithine bird (Aves: Ornithothoraces) from Gansu Province, north-western China |journal=Zoological Journal of the Linnean Society |volume=162 |issue=1 |pages=201–219 |doi=10.1111/j.1096-3642.2010.00671.x |doi-access= free }}</ref>

===Work as an author and educator===
Graffin received the Rushdie Award for Cultural Humanism from the Harvard Humanist Chaplaincy in 2008.<ref>{{cite web|title=Greg Graffin (Bad Religion) talks about humanist award|date=May 21, 2008 |url=http://www.punknews.org/article/28963|access-date=June 23, 2012}}</ref><ref>Archived at [https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211211/w5j9YxpGIPs Ghostarchive]{{cbignore}} and the [https://web.archive.org/web/20201220143147/http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=w5j9YxpGIPs Wayback Machine]{{cbignore}}: {{cite web|title=Greg Graffin's Lifetime Achievement Award Acceptance Speech| website=[[YouTube]] | date=June 8, 2008 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=w5j9YxpGIPs|access-date=June 23, 2012}}{{cbignore}}</ref> 
[[File:Greg Graffin of Bad Religion sings the National Anthem at the Reason Rally. National Mall, Washington, DC, 2012.jpg|thumb|Graffin sings the National Anthem at the [[Reason Rally]], National Mall, Washington, D.C., 2012]]
Throughout 2003, Graffin was engaged in an ongoing email discussion with Preston Jones, a historian at the Christian [[John Brown University]] in [[Arkansas]] and fan of Bad Religion.  The informal philosophical debate that resulted was published as a book titled ''Is Belief in God Good, Bad or Irrelevant? A Professor and Punk Rocker Discuss Science, Religion, Naturalism & Christianity'' in 2006.<ref>{{cite web |author=tor on |url=http://www.pastemagazine.com/articles/2007/08/greg-graffin-punkrock-phd.html |title=Greg Graffin: Punk-Rock Ph.D. |publisher=Paste |date=August 16, 2007 |access-date=2010-10-07 |archive-date=October 10, 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081010055817/http://www.pastemagazine.com/articles/2007/08/greg-graffin-punkrock-phd.html |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.punknews.org/review/6278 |title=Preston Jones / Greg Graffin – Is Belief in God Good, Bad or Irrelevant?|date=May 4, 2007 |work= Punknews.org|access-date=2012-05-12}}</ref>

In 2009, Graffin announced that he had co-written a book with American author [[Steve Olson (writer)|Steve Olson]] titled ''Anarchy Evolution'', released on September 28, 2010 (the same day his band Bad Religion released their 15th album ''[[The Dissent of Man]]'').<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.thebrpage.net/news/?newsID=1618 |title=Graffins new book &#124; News from the front &#124; The Bad Religion Page – Since 1995 |publisher=Thebrpage.net |access-date=2010-10-07}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|title=Anarchy Evolution|publisher=Amazon.ca |date=September 28, 2010 |id= {{ASIN|0061828505|country=ca}}}}</ref> In his book, Graffin writes that he is an [[atheism|atheist]]: "I've never believed in God, which technically makes me an atheist".<ref>{{aut|Graffin, Greg & Olson, Steve}}, Anarchy Evolution: Faith, Science, and Bad Religion in a World Without God. It Books, September 20, 2010. {{ISBN|978-0061828508}}</ref> Although Graffin is not religious, he prefers to identify as a [[Naturalism (philosophy)|naturalist]] rather than as an atheist. "Naturalism is a belief system. A lot of scientists bristle at that. We all have to believe we can find the truth. Evidence is my guide. I rely on observation, experimentation and verification."<ref>{{cite web|last=Draper|first=Electra|title=For punk rocker and professor, Greg Graffin, faith's in the fossil|url=https://www.denverpost.com/news/ci_16600583|publisher=[[The Denver Post]]|access-date=June 23, 2012|date=2010-11-12}}</ref> He also filmed and co-produced a television pilot called ''Punk Professor''.

In 2010, he commented on the project, "It's sitting on someone's shelf waiting to be developed. I'm not actually pursuing it. I said, yeah, I'll shoot the pilot, then it's out of my hands."<ref>{{cite web|last=Chaplinsky|first=Joshua|title=The Naturalistic Worldview of a Punk Rock Professor|url=http://chuckpalahniuk.net/interviews/musicians/greg-graffin-of-bad-religion|publisher=The Cult: The Official [[Chuck Palahniuk]] Website|access-date=June 23, 2012|archive-date=May 1, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120501155831/http://chuckpalahniuk.net/interviews/musicians/greg-graffin-of-bad-religion|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On March 24, 2012, Bad Religion headlined the [[Reason Rally]] in Washington, D.C., where Graffin performed the [[The Star-Spangled Banner|U.S. national anthem]].<ref>{{cite news|url= https://latimesblogs.latimes.com/music_blog/2012/03/reason-rally-bad-religion-washington-dc.html |title=Bad Religion in lineup for March 24 Reason Rally in Washington, D.C. |work=The Los Angeles Times |date=March 21, 2012 |access-date=2012-04-05}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=The Reason Rally Official Schedule|url=http://reasonrally.org/official-schedule/|access-date=June 23, 2012|url-status = dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120617121719/http://reasonrally.org/official-schedule/|archive-date=June 17, 2012|df=mdy-all}}</ref>

In 2014, Graffin received the Humanist Arts Award from the [[American Humanist Association]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Graffin |first1=Greg |title=Into the Fold of Humanism |url=https://thehumanist.com/magazine/november-december-2014/features/into-the-fold-of-humanism |website=The Humanist |publisher=The Humanist |access-date=4 June 2026}}</ref>

Another book entitled ''Population Wars'' was released in September 2015. It had been in the works since at least April 2011 and Graffin spoke about it to be "a bit more in depth about the process of evolution".<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ithaca.com/entertainment/punk-rock-paleontologist-greg-graffin-pursues-music-and-science/article_f9ddc028-6b6f-11e0-be40-001cc4c002e0.html |title=Punk rock paleontologist: Greg Graffin pursues music and science|date=April 20, 2011 |publisher= Ithaca Times|access-date=2016-05-20}}</ref> In a November 2015 interview with ''[[PopMatters]]'' journalist J.C. Maçek III for Graffin's book ''Population Wars'', Graffin stated, "I've made a lot of mistakes, but you can't dwell on mistakes because life is about an adventure. It's about discovery. And you learn from your mistakes so unless you're completely shut down to improving your life, I believe you can continue learning until you're very, very old. You have to look at those past missteps as learning experiences."<ref name=PM>{{cite web|work=[[PopMatters]]|author=Maçek III, J.C.|url=http://www.popmatters.com/feature/adventure-and-discovery-an-academic-discussion-with-bad-religions-greg-graf/|title=Adventure and Discovery, An Academic Discussion With Bad Religion's Greg Graffin|date=24 November 2015}}</ref>
